title: Workload Signature Digest and Gradual Apply Controller
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a recommendation engine that synthesizes compact workload signatures (digest) for each customer route and uses a gradual, monitored apply controller to safely push batching and KV-cache parameters into runtime configs. Goal: reduce per-token cost by 15-30% for eligible workloads while keeping latency and quality SLOs unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Workload digest produced per-route hourly and persisted to profiling store (digest <= 2KB per route)
Recommendation API returns batching and cache parameter set + confidence score for a route
Apply controller supports shadow-canary-rollout with configurable increments (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) and automatic rollback on defined triggers
Dashboards surfaced: digest distribution, recommendation confidence, rollout progress, rollback events
E2E test demonstrating safe rollback when P99 latency increases by > 15ms or error-rate spikes > 0.5%
technical_notes: Digest: use stratified histogram of sequence-lengths (0-32,33-128,129-512,513+), KV cache hit-rate, median/95/99 generation tokens, tokenizer-categorical flags, and average request arrival rate; canonicalize and hash into 256-bit id
Heuristics: cost-model simulates per-token cost under different microbatch sizes and KV cache TTLs; compute expected delta cost and delta P99 latency using measured kernel throughput profiles
Continuous tuning: daily offline replay of sampled traffic (1% sample) to validate recommendations before apply

Safe apply: controller implements shadow traffic (no commit), then canary increments with automatic health checks and pause thresholds; pause criteria are P99 latency +15ms over baseline for > 5 minutes, error-rate delta > 0.5%, or embedding regression on eval set (AUC drop > 1%)
Instrumentation: emit metrics: workload_digest_hash, recommended_microbatch, recommended_kv_ttl_ms, recommendation_confidence, rollout_stage, rollback_reason
Storage: digest store in existing profiling DB (compact column family), TTL 90 days, retention policy for top 1k routes extended to 365 days for trend analysis
decision_log: 2026-02-22: Chose 256-bit digest hash to avoid collisions across millions of routes (Tomasz + Priya)
2026-02-25: Opted for stratified sequence-length buckets instead of raw histograms to reduce storage and make rules stable (Marcus)
2026-03-02: Rollout increment schedule standardized to 1%, 5%, 25%, 100% with 30m observation windows between steps; can be overridden per-customer (PM feedback)
2026-03-08: Added embedding-quality check to rollback triggers after product flagged potential semantic regressions in early experiments (Riley)
2026-03-10: Agreed to surface recommendation confidence (low/medium/high) and require manual approval for low-confidence high-impact routes
implementation_steps: 1) Profiling job: implement route digest generator in profiler-service; run hourly; store digest in profiling DB
2) Cost simulator: offline tool that maps digest -> recommended microbatch / kv-ttl using kernel-performance table
3) Recommendation API: read digest and simulator output, respond with parameter set + confidence and rationale
4) Apply controller: implement shadow canary flows that can push configs to runtime with staged percentages and health-probes
5) Telemetry & dashboards: add metrics to telemetry pipeline, Grafana panels for rollout health and per-route recommendations
6) Safety tests & e2e: create synthetic workloads and acceptance tests that validate rollback triggers and no-regression in latency/quality
